models.name: discussion_board_guests
models.description:
Guest visitors who browse the discussion board without authentication.

Guests represent unauthenticated users who can view published articles, read comments, and browse public content. They are tracked for analytics purposes to understand visitor behavior and traffic patterns.

Guests cannot create content, post comments, or interact with the platform beyond read-only operations. To gain full participation capabilities, guests must register as members.

This table tracks guest browsing sessions for analytics and monitoring purposes, helping identify conversion opportunities from guest to member registration.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the guest visitor for tracking and analytics purposes.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current page URL being accessed by the guest.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating where the guest came from.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session was first created.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description:
Registered members who actively participate in discussions.

Members are authenticated users who have completed registration and email verification. They can create articles with rich content including images and file attachments, write comments on any published article, and manage their own content.

Each member has unique authentication credentials (email and password) allowing secure login access. The system tracks member account status to support suspension capabilities for moderation purposes.

Members represent the core user base of the discussion board, contributing content and engaging in economic and political discussions. Their profiles display contribution history including article and comment counts.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Member email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all members.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for member authentication. Stored using bcrypt with minimum cost factor of 10.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Display name shown on articles, comments, and profile pages. Must be unique across all members.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account status for moderation purposes. Valid values: active, suspended, locked. Active accounts have full access, suspended accounts are temporarily restricted by moderators, locked accounts are temporarily frozen due to security concerns.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the member has verified their email address. Members must verify email before gaining full access to the platform.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created (registration date).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account information was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for registered members.

Tracks active login sessions for members to enable secure authentication and session management. Each session represents a member's authenticated connection to the platform from a specific device or browser.

Sessions include connection context (IP address, access URL, referrer) for security monitoring and audit purposes. The expired_at timestamp allows for session expiration and timeout handling.

This table supports JWT token refresh workflows and enables features like logout from all devices by invalidating all user sessions.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the member established this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating where the member came from when starting the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (login time).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated. Null indicates an active session.

models.name: discussion_board_moderators
models.description:
Moderators who maintain community standards and manage the platform.

Moderators are trusted administrators with elevated privileges to manage content and enforce community guidelines. They can edit or delete any article or comment, manage user accounts including suspension capabilities, and access moderation dashboards.

Each moderator has unique authentication credentials (email and password) for secure administrative access. Moderators have all capabilities of regular members plus comprehensive moderation tools.

Moderators ensure discussions remain civil, on-topic, and compliant with community standards. They review reported content, handle user account issues, and maintain the overall quality of the discussion board.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Moderator email address used for authentication and administrative communication. Must be unique across all moderators.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for moderator authentication. Stored using bcrypt with minimum cost factor of 10.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Display name shown when moderators take actions or interact with the platform. Must be unique across all moderators.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account information was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for moderators.

Tracks active login sessions for moderators to enable secure administrative access and session management. Each session represents a moderator's authenticated connection for performing moderation duties.

Sessions include connection context (IP address, access URL, referrer) for security auditing and monitoring of administrative actions. The expired_at timestamp allows for session expiration and timeout handling.

This table supports JWT token refresh workflows for moderators and enables security features like logout from all devices by invalidating all moderator sessions. Critical for maintaining audit trails of administrative access.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the moderator established this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating where the moderator came from when starting the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (moderator login time).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated. Null indicates an active moderator session.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Core content entity representing articles published by members for economic and political discussions.

Articles are the primary business value of the discussion board, allowing members to share comprehensive analysis, perspectives, and arguments on economic policies and political developments. Each article contains a title and body content with support for rich text formatting.

Articles are created by authenticated members through their active sessions and immediately published for public viewing by all users including guests. The author can edit their articles at any time, and moderators can edit or remove any article for community standards enforcement.

The view_count field tracks how many times an article has been accessed, providing engagement metrics. Articles support attachments through separate image and file entities, enabling evidence-based discussions with supporting materials like charts, data, and reference documents.

Soft deletion is supported through deleted_at to maintain discussion continuity when content is moderated or removed, preserving references from comments and other entities while hiding content from public view.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Author who created this article. References the member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Authentication session through which this article was created. References the session's {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id} for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title summarizing the topic or main argument. Must be between 5 and 200 characters to ensure meaningful yet concise titles.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full article content containing the member's analysis, arguments, and discussion points. Supports rich text formatting including paragraphs and line breaks. Must be between 10 and 50,000 characters to ensure substantive content.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this article has been viewed by any user including guests. Incremented each time the article detail page is accessed, providing engagement metrics.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was originally created and published. Preserved permanently even when article is edited.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent edit to the article. Updated whenever the title, body, or attachments are modified by the author or a moderator.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the article was removed by the author or a moderator. When set, the article is hidden from public view but preserved in the database to maintain referential integrity with comments and audit trails.

models.name: discussion_board_article_images
models.description:
Image attachments enriching articles with visual supporting content.

Stores uploaded images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP formats) that members attach to articles to provide visual evidence, charts, graphs, infographics, or illustrative content. Each image is associated with exactly one parent article and is managed through article creation and editing workflows.

The system enforces a maximum of 10 images per article with individual file size limit of 10 MB. Images are validated for format and integrity before storage. When articles are deleted, all associated images are removed from storage.

Image metadata includes original filename for user reference, file size for storage tracking, content type for proper browser rendering, and storage URL for retrieval. Creation timestamp tracks when images were uploaded.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article that this image attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded image as provided by the user. Preserved for user reference and download purposes. May contain file extension indicating image format.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the image file in bytes. Used for storage tracking and enforcing the 10 MB maximum file size limit. Must be positive integer value.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the image file for proper browser rendering. Valid values include image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp corresponding to supported formats.

plainFields.name: storage_url
plainFields.description: URL or storage path where the image file is stored. Used by the system to retrieve and serve the image to users viewing the article. May be CDN URL or internal storage path.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Width of the image in pixels. Captured during upload for display optimization and layout calculations. Null if dimensions could not be determined.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Height of the image in pixels. Captured during upload for display optimization and layout calculations. Null if dimensions could not be determined.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image was uploaded to the system. Tracks upload time for audit trail and chronological ordering of attachments.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image was soft deleted. Null if the image is currently active. Enables recovery and audit trail before permanent removal from storage.

models.name: discussion_board_article_files
models.description:
Document file attachments providing supporting evidence and reference materials for articles.

Stores uploaded document files (PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV, ZIP formats) that members attach to articles to provide supporting data, research papers, spreadsheets, policy documents, or other reference materials. Each file is associated with exactly one parent article and is managed through article creation and editing workflows.

The system enforces a maximum of 5 files per article with individual file size limit of 25 MB. Files are validated for format and scanned for integrity before storage. When articles are deleted, all associated files are removed from storage.

File metadata includes original filename for user reference and download, file size for storage tracking and limit enforcement, content type for proper browser handling and download behavior, and storage URL for retrieval. Creation timestamp tracks when files were uploaded for audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article that this file attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded document as provided by the user. Preserved for user reference and used as download filename. Includes file extension indicating document type.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the document file in bytes. Used for storage tracking and enforcing the 25 MB maximum file size limit. Must be positive integer value.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the document file for proper browser handling and download behavior. Examples include application/pdf, application/msword, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, text/plain, text/csv, application/zip corresponding to supported formats.

plainFields.name: storage_url
plainFields.description: URL or storage path where the document file is stored. Used by the system to retrieve and serve the file for download to users. May be CDN URL or internal storage path.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded to the system. Tracks upload time for audit trail and chronological ordering of attachments.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was soft deleted. Null if the file is currently active. Enables recovery and audit trail before permanent removal from storage.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
User comments on discussion board articles.

Stores community member comments and discussions on published articles. Each comment is created by an authenticated member and associated with a specific article. Comments enable engagement and conversation around economic and political topics.

Comments support independent management operations including cross-article search for user activity tracking, moderation workflows for content review, and direct edit or delete actions by comment authors or moderators.

The comment content is limited to 2000 characters as specified in requirements. Comments are displayed chronologically by creation time to maintain discussion flow.

Soft deletion is supported through the deleted_at field to preserve discussion context while allowing content moderation. Moderators can remove inappropriate comments while maintaining the overall discussion thread integrity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who created this comment. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Comment text content. Contains the member's written response or discussion contribution to the article. Limited to 2000 characters as per requirements. Supports line breaks and basic text formatting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was created. Used for chronological ordering of comments within article discussions.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last modified. Updated whenever the comment content is edited by the author or moderator.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates the comment has been removed by the author or moderator. Supports content moderation while preserving discussion context.
